# IKControl

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("IKControl")`

Bends a limb so its end reaches a target, or turns a head to look at one, on top of the animation that is playing. Use it to put a hand on a weapon's grip or a foot on a pedal, or to make eyes follow something. Parent it to the skinned `MeshPart`, set `EndJoint` to the joint at the end of the limb (the hand, the foot or the head), and set `Target`.

It is visual only. Each machine solves it every frame for the pose it draws; it does not change the pose that simulation code reads, so a `Bone` on the hand still reports where the clip put it. To turn a joint in a way that game logic can read, use `Bone.Transform`. Anything drawn with the limb follows it, such as a part attached to one of its bones.

A limb reaches no farther than its length. In a multiplayer match, the control and its properties replicate with the character, and each machine does the bending itself.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AlignRotation` | `boolean` | — | read/write | For `TwoBone`: whether the end joint also takes the target's rotation, so a palm lies flat on a grip or a sole lies flat on a pedal. |
| `ChainLength` | `number` | `2` | read/write | For `LookAt`: how many joints above the end joint share the turn, from 0 to 8. With 0 only the head turns; with 2, the head, the neck and one spine joint each take an equal share. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the control is applied. A disabled control costs nothing. |
| `EndJoint` | `string` | — | read/write | The name of the joint at the end of the limb, as it is named in the model file: a hand, a foot or a head. The control does nothing if the rig has no joint of that name. |
| `MaxAngle` | `number` | `70` | read/write | For `LookAt`: the largest angle, in degrees, that the look can turn away from straight ahead. Beyond it, the look stops at the limit. |
| `Pole` | `(BasePart | Attachment)?` | — | read/write | For `TwoBone`: the part or attachment the elbow or knee points toward. With none, the limb bends the way the animation already bends it. |
| `Smoothing` | `number` | `0.1` | read/write | The time, in seconds, over which a sudden change is eased, such as a target that jumps or the control being enabled. At 0 the control follows immediately. |
| `Target` | `(BasePart | Attachment)?` | — | read/write | The part or attachment to reach for or look at. The control uses the position where the target is drawn in the current frame. With no target, the control does nothing. |
| `TargetOffset` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | An offset from the target, in the target's own space. Use it to aim at a point on the target, such as a grip a hand's width from the middle of a weapon. |
| `Type` | `Enum.IKControlType` | `Enum.IKControlType.TwoBone` | read/write | What the control does. `TwoBone` treats the end joint and the two joints above it as a limb and moves the end to the target. `LookAt` turns the end joint to face the target; the joints above it share the turn. |
| `Weight` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How strongly the control is applied, from 0 to 1. At 0 only the animation shows. Tween it to blend the control in and out smoothly. |
